title: WPMS/1355/2018 of M/s Nectafresh Agro Foods Vs Uttarakhand Environment Protection and Pollution Control Board

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1355 Of 2018

M/s Nectafresh Agro Foods Ö Petitioner
Versus
Uttarakhand Environment Protection & Pollution
Control Board Ö Respondent
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. Shiv Pandey, Advocate, holding brief of Mr.
Anurag Bisaria, Advocate for the respondent.

Petitionerís factory has been closed by the
order dated 18.4.2018 passed by the Uttarakhand
Environment Protection and Pollution Control Board
(from hereinafter referred to as the ëBoardí).
Admittedly, an inspection of the petitionerís factory
was carried out on 28.3.2018 and it was found that
the petitionerís factory does not have the Effluent
Treatment Plant in working condition. Subsequently,
the respondent Board passed an order dated
18.4.2018 under Section 33-A of the Water
(Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
directing the petitioner to close down the factory.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has preferred the
present writ petition before this Court.

2. Although, the order dated 18.4.2018 is
appellable under Section 33-B of the Water
(Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, but

2
the ground raised by the petitioner before this Court
is that sub-rule (3) of Rule 34 of the Rules framed
under the Act, provides that before issuing any
direction under Section 33-A of the Water (Prevention
and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 at least 15 daysí
prior notice shall be given to the person concerned.
Admittedly, it has not been done in the present case.
It is also the case of the petitioner that on the date
when the inspection was carried out, the petitionerís
factory was closed on that day and so was the Water
Treatment Plant.
3. Learned Counsel for the respondent relied
upon sub-rule (6) of Rule 34 which provides that in
case where the Board is of the opinion that there is
likelihood of imminent danger to the environment,
this notice may be dispensed with but with the
reasons to be recorded in writing for dispensing with
such notice. However, in the impugned order no such
reason or finding is given, as contemplated under
sub-rule (6) of Rule 34 of the Water (Prevention and
Control of Pollution) Rules, 1975.
4. Considering that since the respondent has
closed the factory of the petitioner without providing
an opportunity of hearing and since Rule 34 has not
been complied with and presently the petitionerís
factory is lying closed, let a hearing be given to the
petitioner by the respondent. The petitioner shall
apprise all relevant facts to the respondent and
thereafter the Uttarakhand Environment Protection &
Pollution Control Board shall take fresh decision and
pass the order afresh under Section 33-A of the

3
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
In case, the respondent Board comes to the
conclusion that the factor is actually polluting the
environment, closure order, as contemplated under
Section 33-A of the Water (Prevention and Control of
Pollution) Act, 1974, shall be passed. Since the order
has to be passed afresh, the respondent Board is
directed to consider all the relevant parameters as
well as pleas of the petitioner and then pass a
speaking and reasoned order. It is made clear that till
the fresh order is passed by the respondent Board,
the petitionerís factory shall remain closed and it
shall be opened only in case the petitionerís
representation is decided in his favour.
5. With the directions/observations as above,
the writ petition stands disposed of.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 09.7.2018
